articles.title: Trump Threatens EU With 'Very Heavy Tariffs' Over Canada Associate Membership
articles.excerpt: Hours after Ursula von der Leyen proposed making Canada the EU's first associate member, Trump called it "laughable" and warned of tariffs — unless Europe's intentions are "good."
articles.image_caption: US President Donald Trump. On September 17, 2026, Trump warned the European Union of very heavy tariffs if it makes Canada an associate member with what he called bad intention.
articles.nri_angle: Canada hosts one of the world's largest Indian diasporas; a deeper EU-Canada corridor could open new trade and mobility pathways, while fresh US tariffs would ripple through global supply chains Indian exporters rely on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: House Passes Graham Russia Sanctions Bill 262-159, Putting India in 100% Tariff Crosshairs
articles.excerpt: Named for the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, the package authorises President Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100% on the top importers of Russian energy; the Kremlin said Thursday the move would 'complicate' Ukraine peace efforts.
articles.image_caption: The dome of the US Capitol in Washington, DC, with the American flag flying. The House of Representatives passed the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act by 262-159 on Wednesday, sending it to President Trump for his signature.
articles.nri_angle: India is directly in the bill's crosshairs — New Delhi's Russian oil purchases could expose Indian exports to tariffs of up to 100%, and India has already warned Washington that such measures would damage bilateral ties.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Warns US That New Tariffs Over Russian Oil Could Damage Ties
articles.excerpt: Hours after the US House passed a bill authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on top Russian oil buyers, New Delhi cautioned Washington that the move could strain the bilateral relationship and vowed to protect its energy security.
articles.image_caption: An image from Mint's coverage of US-India trade relations. India warned on September 17 that a US House bill authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on buyers of Russian oil could damage bilateral ties.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora, the standoff touches Indian-American importers, energy and trade professionals, and the US-India commercial corridor, all of which would feel the impact if the tariff weapon is actually deployed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Finneas, Other Acts Quit Ed Sheeran Tour After Macklemore Ousted Over Palestine
articles.excerpt: Finneas, Aaron Rowe, Lukas Graham and Sheeran's own touring band Beoga walked out on Tuesday, accusing stadium owners led by Robert Kraft of silencing the rapper's onstage "Free Palestine" remarks.
articles.image_caption: Singer-songwriter and producer Finneas O'Connell. He quit Ed Sheeran's Loop Tour after Macklemore was dropped from the lineup.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian-diaspora readers, the fallout is another reminder of how sharply pro-Palestinian speech is policed on Western pop's biggest stages.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Von der Leyen Pledges EU 'Counter-Hybrid Playbook,' Offers Canada Associate Membership
articles.excerpt: In a 73-minute State of the Union address in Strasbourg, the European Commission president unveiled a European 'Article 4' emergency security protocol, a tougher stance on China, and a frontier-AI pact — warning that threats are mounting on European soil.
articles.image_caption: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. She proposed a 'counter-hybrid playbook' for EU states facing sabotage and drone incursions.
articles.nri_angle: The speech signals tighter EU borders and faster migrant returns alongside expanded legal migration channels and skills initiatives, a mix that matters for the Indian professionals and students who form one of the largest migrant communities in several EU states.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Galwan War Film's Long Road Shows India's Softening Line on China
articles.excerpt: Salman Khan's Maatrubhumi — announced as Battle of Galwan — has been stalled by a defence ministry directive as India recalibrates its China policy, and TRT World says the saga reads like a barometer of that thaw.
articles.nri_angle: The saga shows how New Delhi's China reset is reaching beyond diplomacy into the stories Bollywood is allowed to tell — a shift diaspora audiences will feel on screen before they see it in policy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amazon Wants 1,000 Same-Day Delivery Hubs Within 10 Miles of Prime Members
articles.excerpt: Codenamed Project Mercury, the internal plan would grow Amazon's same-day footprint from 85 sites to more than 1,000 by 2031, placing hubs within a 10-mile radius of 80% of US Prime subscribers. Amazon says the projections are preliminary and subject to revision.
articles.image_caption: An Amazon fulfillment center. Amazon is planning an internal initiative, codenamed Project Mercury, to expand its same-day delivery network from about 85 facilities to more than 1,000 sites by 2031.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian-American families who rely on Amazon for everything from weekly groceries to festival-season essentials, a same-day hub within a 10-mile radius would narrow the last real advantage of the neighborhood store.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: War-Damaged Gaza Apartment Block Collapses, Killing at Least 20
articles.excerpt: The al-Sa'ada building in Gaza City's Rimal neighborhood collapsed overnight with about 100 people believed trapped, exposing the perilous living conditions of displaced Palestinians as reconstruction remains stalled.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian readers following the war's humanitarian toll, the collapse shows how Gaza's destruction keeps claiming lives beyond the battlefield, through the damaged buildings displaced families are forced to shelter in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cabinet Raises EPFO Wage Ceiling to ₹25,000 After 12 Years
articles.excerpt: The Union Cabinet's decision to lift the mandatory EPFO coverage ceiling from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 a month will bring over 51 lakh more workers into provident fund, pension and insurance coverage from September 17.
articles.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs hold dormant EPF accounts from earlier India stints, and families back home in the ₹15,000–₹25,000 band now gain retirement savings, pension eligibility and insurance protection.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Houthis Claim Missile Strike on Aramco Facilities in Yanbu
articles.excerpt: The unverified claim targets Saudi Arabia's main Red Sea oil port — the linchpin of Riyadh's crude rerouting around the closed Strait of Hormuz — as Brent climbs to $107.80.
articles.image_caption: A Houthi military spokesman addresses a press conference. The Houthis claimed a missile strike on Aramco facilities in Yanbu, Saudi Arabia.
articles.nri_angle: India, the world's third-largest oil importer, absorbs every Brent price spike into its import bill and fuel prices — and Red Sea disruption hits the route carrying much of its Gulf crude.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gold Mine Collapse in Sudan's West Kordofan Kills at Least 60
articles.excerpt: The al-Zara artisanal mine disaster — with up to 82 dead reported and dozens missing — is the latest deadly collapse in a gold sector that funds Sudan's civil war.
articles.image_caption: An artisanal gold miner rests on a wheelbarrow at a mine in Eastern Uganda. A shaft collapse at an informal artisanal mine in West Kordofan, Sudan, killed at least 60 people.
articles.nri_angle: India is one of the world's largest gold consumers, and Sudan's artisanal gold — much of it smuggled through Dubai — feeds the same global supply chains that end in Indian jewelry markets.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Coast Guard, FBI Boarded Two Texas-Bound Tankers After Cyberattacks
articles.excerpt: The August 21 and 24 boardings followed suspected breaches of the ships' networks near the Strait of Gibraltar; officials are probing a possible Iran link but have not named a culprit.
articles.image_caption: A U.S. Coast Guard member watches an oil tanker at sea. The Coast Guard and FBI boarded two Texas-bound tankers following reported cyberattacks.
articles.nri_angle: India moves most of its energy imports by sea and its IT firms run much of the world's ship-management software — the same integrated ship systems that were breached here.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Senate Blocks Landmark Crypto Bill as Bitcoin Tumbles 4%
articles.excerpt: The CLARITY Act's 49-50 cloture defeat on Tuesday marks the crypto industry's first major legislative loss since it spent over $300 million on the 2024 and 2026 elections.
articles.image_caption: President Donald Trump walks near a helicopter. The Senate blocked landmark crypto legislation as Bitcoin tumbled 4%.
articles.nri_angle: India remains one of the world's largest retail crypto markets, so U.S. regulatory clarity — now delayed at least a year — directly affects the rulebook for exchanges serving Indian and NRI investors.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India Crew Member's Missed Ganpati Puja Found Her at 35,000 Feet
articles.excerpt: Anuradha Soni thought her flight roster had cost her the family's Ganpati Puja. Then a passenger boarded with a Ganesha idol — and the celebration came to her.
articles.image_caption: Air India cabin crew member Anuradha Soni with the Ganpati idol carried aboard her flight. A passenger had brought the idol along, letting her perform the Ganpati Puja she had missed at home.
articles.nri_angle: Air India is the diaspora's bridge home, and this story of a missed festival being found at 35,000 feet speaks directly to NRIs who routinely celebrate Ganesh Chaturthi thousands of miles from family.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India Board Convenes in Mumbai as New CEO Gebremariam Prepares to Take Charge
articles.excerpt: Directors led by N. Chandrasekaran met at Bombay House to set the pay package for incoming chief Tewolde Gebremariam and formalize the handover from outgoing CEO Campbell Wilson.
articles.image_caption: Incoming Air India CEO Tewolde Gebremariam (left) and outgoing CEO Campbell Wilson (right). The Air India board met in Mumbai to discuss Gebremariam pay package as he prepares to take charge.
articles.nri_angle: Air India remains the default carrier for many NRIs on India routes, so a stable leadership handover and a chief visibly accountable for safety and on-time performance matter directly to diaspora flyers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: San Jose Woman Arrested on Hate Crime Charges After Accusing Dad of Trafficking Daughter
articles.excerpt: The 47-year-old was booked into Santa Clara County jail on suspicion of stalking and hate crimes after a viral video showed her confronting a father in San Jose's Almaden neighborhood over his 6-year-old daughter.
articles.image_caption: The Almaden neighborhood in San Jose, where the September 6 confrontation took place. The father filmed the encounter and posted it on TikTok before the woman was arrested.
articles.nri_angle: Immigrant and South Asian families in the Bay Area see the case as a warning about how racial assumptions can turn a family outing into a police matter.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Anthropic Says It Blocked Russian Bid to Build Killer Drone Swarm
articles.excerpt: The company says a Russia-based group used Claude to engineer autonomous drones able to pick targets — including people — and detonate without human approval.
articles.image_caption: Image: @OwenGregorian via X
articles.nri_angle: The weaponisation of Western AI by Russia is a core geopolitical story for a diaspora readership that follows the Ukraine war, India-Russia ties, and the AI safety debate closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Consumer Regulator Escalates Apple Probe Over iOS 18 Warranty Terms
articles.excerpt: The Central Consumer Protection Authority has ordered a detailed investigation into complaints that the iOS 18 update damaged iPhone screens, leaving users with repair bills of up to Rs 27,900.
articles.image_caption: iPhones on display at an Apple retail store. India’s Central Consumer Protection Authority has escalated its probe into Apple’s software warranty terms over complaints linked to the iOS 18 update.
articles.nri_angle: Indian consumers and the large diaspora who buy iPhones in India or send them to family will be watching whether the probe leads to refunds or rewritten warranty terms.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Odisha Rejects Premature Release of Dara Singh in Graham Staines Murder Case
articles.excerpt: The State Sentence Review Board rejected the premature release plea on law-and-order grounds, after the Supreme Court repeatedly pressed Odisha to decide without further delay.
articles.image_caption: A corridor of barred cells inside an Indian prison. Odisha’s Sentence Review Board has rejected Dara Singh’s plea for premature release on law-and-order grounds.

sources.label: Bar & Bench (Sentence Review Board pulled up)
LiveLaw (SC pulls up Odisha over delay)
LawBeat (SC asks Odisha to decide by Aug 19)

articles.nri_angle: The Staines murders drew sustained international attention given the Australian identity of the victims; diaspora and religious-freedom watchers track how India handles remission for high-profile sectarian crimes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Lawmaker Seeks to Name India in Russia Sanctions Bill Authorizing 100% Tariffs
articles.excerpt: Democratic Congressman Steny Hoyer's amendment would explicitly list India among ten countries eligible for up to 100% duties, as the House races a four-day clock before its pre-midterm recess.
articles.nri_angle: Explicitly naming India in the sanctions bill would put Indian exporters' U.S. market access — textiles, pharma, gems — directly at risk, making the House markup a high-stakes watch for the Indian-American business community.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin Woman, Friend Killed by Subway Train in Lower Manhattan
articles.excerpt: Malaika Chitre, 24, of Dayton, New Jersey, and Navam Kaul, 24, of Sayreville, were struck by a southbound No. 4 train around 3:15 a.m. Sunday at the Spring Street station; police are investigating how they ended up on the tracks.
articles.image_caption: The Spring Street station platform on the 4/6 line in Lower Manhattan. Malaika Chitre, 24, of Dayton, New Jersey, and her friend Navam Kaul, 24, of Sayreville, were struck by a southbound No. 4 train here around 3:15 a.m. Sunday.
articles.nri_angle: The deaths of two 24-year-old New Jersey friends — an Indian-origin woman and a Nepali-American man — have shaken the South Asian community in the New York region, where both grew up and graduated from Rutgers in 2024.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Saudi Arabia Warns of 'Firm' Response After Houthi Attacks Wound 13
articles.excerpt: Riyadh vowed a firm response to Yemen's Houthis after ballistic missile and drone attacks on the kingdom's south, as emergency alerts rang across six cities including the Red Sea oil port of Yanbu.
articles.image_caption: The Riyadh skyline, Saudi Arabia. The kingdom warned of a 'firm' response after Houthi ballistic missile and drone attacks wounded 13 civilians in the country's south.
articles.nri_angle: Saudi Arabia hosts one of the world's largest Indian expatriate communities, and a widening conflict puts the safety of millions of Indian workers — and the remittances their families depend on — directly at risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Gavi Says New TB Vaccines From 2029 Could Save 7.3 Million Lives
articles.excerpt: Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, says novel tuberculosis vaccines expected from 2029 could avert up to 7.3 million deaths by 2050 and unlock $135 billion in economic benefits — if supply reaches the countries that need them most.
articles.image_caption: A TB ward in a hospital. Gavi says new TB vaccines arriving from 2029 could save 7.3 million lives.
articles.nri_angle: India carries the world's largest tuberculosis burden by WHO estimates, so supply and pricing of the new vaccines will directly affect Indian health systems and families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bangladesh's Measles Death Toll Crosses 1,000 as Outbreak Rages On
articles.excerpt: Six months after it began, Bangladesh's measles outbreak — the largest in the world, per the CDC — has killed more than 1,000 people, nearly all children, as vaccination gaps and a faltering immunization program fuel the spread.
articles.nri_angle: Bangladesh's large diaspora in the US, UK, and Canada — and families traveling to South Asia — should note the outbreak's scale; checking MMR vaccination status before travel is the simplest precaution.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indonesian Firefighters Teach Fire Safety Set to 'Saajan Ji Ghar Aaye' in Viral Videos
articles.excerpt: Fire and rescue crews in Makassar, Indonesia have gone viral for demonstrating how to handle kitchen and gas-cylinder fires while Bollywood songs play — turning a routine safety drill into the internet's favorite music video.
articles.image_caption: Firefighters work to contain peatland fires in South Sumatra, Indonesia, during the country's severe wildfire season. Health officials say more than 50,000 respiratory infections have been linked to the fires so far.
articles.nri_angle: Indonesian firefighters' Bollywood-set safety videos show Bollywood's durable cultural reach across Southeast Asia — home culture surfacing untranslated and immediately understood in an unexpected place.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India, Canada Open Fourth Round of Talks on Proposed Trade Pact
articles.excerpt: The five-day round in New Delhi covering goods, services and rules of origin aims to conclude the Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement by the end of 2026, with both sides targeting $50 billion in bilateral trade by 2030.
articles.nri_angle: With over 425,000 Indian students and a large Indian-origin community in Canada, CEPA's services and mobility chapters land directly on diaspora jobs, businesses, and remittance costs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India to Supply 654 MW Power Daily to Flood-Ravaged Nepal
articles.excerpt: New Delhi's Ministry of Power cleared 18-hour daily electricity exports to the Nepal Electricity Authority through December 31, after August floods erased about a tenth of Nepal's hydropower capacity.
articles.nri_angle: For South Asian diaspora communities — especially Nepalis living and working in India — India's rapid power supply and relief response demonstrates New Delhi acting as first responder when an open-border neighbour is hit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's 7.8% Growth Beats Forecasts — But Few Indians Feel It
articles.excerpt: The June-quarter print smashed expectations, yet economists and critics question the numbers and point to weak jobs, uneven consumption and a fight over the data methodology.
articles.image_caption: Dice spelling out GDP with an upward arrow, arranged by hand. India's economy grew 7.8% last quarter, but many Indians say the headline number has not translated into better living standards.
articles.nri_angle: The growth-versus-jobs debate shapes the economic reality that diaspora readers' families in India live with.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Xi Pledges China Will Lead AI, Tech Cooperation Push for BRICS
articles.excerpt: At the BRICS leaders' summit in New Delhi, China's president unveiled a 'Greater BRICS Initiative' including a BRICS AI Open Source Zone, a special economic zone partnership and a service trade forum.
articles.image_caption: Chinese President Xi Jinping at an official engagement in July 2024. Xi pledged that China would lead a push for greater AI and technology cooperation among BRICS nations.
articles.nri_angle: India holds the 2026 BRICS chair, placing New Delhi at the center of the bloc's AI and trade agenda.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kremlin Says Modi and Xi Offered Putin Help to End Ukraine War
articles.excerpt: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the leaders of India and China offered their 'good offices' to help find a settlement during bilateral meetings with Vladimir Putin in New Delhi ahead of the BRICS summit.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin at the BRICS summit. The Kremlin said Modi and Xi offered to help Putin work toward ending the war in Ukraine.
articles.nri_angle: India's potential mediating role in the Ukraine war puts New Delhi's diplomacy at the center of a story diaspora readers follow closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: More Than 129 Missing After Indonesian Ferry Overturns in Java Sea
articles.excerpt: The Virgo Transport 8, carrying 243 people from Surabaya to Banjarmasin, capsized in rough seas early Sunday. Rescuers have saved 108 people and recovered six bodies as a dozen vessels and two helicopters comb the Java Sea.
articles.image_caption: Indonesian search-and-rescue officers coordinate operations at a command post. More than 129 people remain missing after a passenger ferry overturned in the Java Sea.
articles.nri_angle: A major maritime disaster of broad interest to The Videshi's global readership; no India-specific angle.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Stalked for Months, Reported Again and Again: Indian-Origin Woman Shot Dead in Sacramento
articles.excerpt: Shalini Thakur, 38, had told Sacramento deputies about a tracker hidden in her car and secured a restraining order months before she was killed. The suspect was later found dead after a freeway standoff.
articles.image_caption: The Sacramento skyline. Indian-origin waitress Shalini Thakur, 38, was shot and killed in a Sacramento parking lot on September 8 after months of reported stalking.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-origin woman was killed in California after months of documented stalking, raising diaspora concerns about victim safety, and the suspect's immigration history has made the case a U.S. enforcement debate flashpoint.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India and China Can Build a Multipolar World, Says Economist Jeffrey Sachs
articles.excerpt: The Columbia economist told India Today that within 25 years, India and China will be the world's two largest economies, and that closer cooperation between them could anchor a genuinely multilateral order.
articles.image_caption: The flags of India and China with an inset photo of economist Jeffrey Sachs. Sachs told India Today that India will become the world largest economy at some point this century.
articles.nri_angle: Sachs' forecast reinforces the long-term growth case for India that many NRIs are already investing behind, while his critique of US tariffs speaks to diaspora concerns about the bilateral relationship.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Meets Tokayev, El-Sisi as Xi and Putin Depart After BRICS Summit
articles.excerpt: On the final day of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, the prime minister held bilateral talks with Kazakhstan's Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Egypt's Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, as the summit adopted the New Delhi Declaration and Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin departed.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He held bilateral talks with Kazakhstan's Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Egypt's Abdel Fattah El-Sisi on the final day of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi.
articles.nri_angle: India's turn chairing an expanded BRICS puts New Delhi's trade, energy and currency decisions at the centre of the Global South's agenda, with ripple effects on the global markets in which diaspora savings and investments sit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amit Shah Sets 2029 Deadline for Uniform Civil Code in 21 NDA-Ruled States
articles.excerpt: Speaking in Mumbai, the Union home minister said BJP-led NDA governments in 21 states would introduce a common civil code before the 2029 Lok Sabha elections, and announced a month-long campaign marking Narendra Modi's 25 years in public life.
articles.image_caption: Union Home Minister Amit Shah. He said all 21 NDA-ruled states will implement the Uniform Civil Code before the 2029 general elections.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs with property and family ties in India, a common code governing inheritance and succession across states could simplify estate matters, though the rollout is several years out.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin Surrey Landlady Arrested After Tenant's Viral Harassment Videos
articles.excerpt: Raj Tiwana was taken into custody by Surrey Police after a tenant documented alleged harassment, unauthorized entries, and physical confrontations in videos that spread widely online. Police have issued no official statement, and the exact charges remain unclear.
articles.image_caption: Two Surrey Police officers escort a handcuffed woman outside a house in Surrey, British Columbia. The woman is Raj Tiwana, the Indian-origin landlady taken into custody after her tenant posted viral videos alleging harassment and unauthorized entry at the rental property.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-origin landlady's arrest in Canada shows diaspora landlords must follow provincial tenancy law, not personal confrontation, when disputes arise.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Indian-Origin Woman Charged With Two First-Degree Murders in California Killings
articles.excerpt: Anila Baby, 32, allegedly killed two friends from Kerala in separate attacks about 90 minutes apart on August 28, and faces 50 years to life in prison if convicted.
articles.image_caption: Anila Baby in a booking photo. The 32-year-old is charged with two counts of first-degree murder in the killings of two friends in San Jose and Milpitas, California.
articles.nri_angle: The double homicide in the South Bay has shaken the Bay Area's large Malayali community, where the accused and both victims lived.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CDC Declares Record Lettuce-Linked Parasite Outbreak Over After 12,883 Cases
articles.excerpt: The multistate cyclosporiasis outbreak tied to Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce is the largest on record; the FDA's contamination investigation continues.
articles.image_caption: A shopper browses packaged salad blends and bagged greens in a grocery store refrigerated produce case. The CDC has declared the record cyclosporiasis outbreak linked to recalled Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce over.
articles.nri_angle: With fresh produce central to South Asian cooking, the outbreak is a reminder to wash leafy greens thoroughly and heed federal recall notices promptly.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: After Talks Until 4 AM, BRICS Reaches Consensus With India's Help
articles.excerpt: Negotiators hammered out a joint declaration condemning unilateral war after all-night consultations led by India, bridging deep divisions between Iran and the UAE over the Gulf conflict.
articles.nri_angle: The UAE and Saudi Arabia are among the largest destinations for Indian workers abroad, so India's role in bridging the Iran-UAE divide directly protects the diaspora's jobs, remittance corridors, and travel routes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Pushes for BRICS Bank Membership as Araghchi Calls Modi Talks 'Strong'
articles.excerpt: On the sidelines of the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, Iran's foreign minister said Tehran is “working on” New Development Bank membership, with some countries already supportive.
articles.image_caption: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi. He called his talks with Prime Minister Modi 'strong' as Iran pushes for BRICS bank membership.
articles.nri_angle: A deeper India-Iran economic partnership, via Chabahar and local-currency trade, matters to Indian businesses and diaspora professionals engaged in Gulf and West Asia commerce.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Xi's Mystery Black-Covered Limousine Lands in Delhi Ahead of BRICS Summit
articles.excerpt: The Hongqi N701, China's secretive presidential limousine, arrived under covers for Xi Jinping's first India visit in seven years, with Modi set to host him on Saturday evening.
articles.image_caption: Chinese President Xi Jinping. His black-covered limousine drew attention as he landed in Delhi for the BRICS summit.
articles.nri_angle: The summit's outcomes on trade, currency settlement, and India-China ties will shape the economic environment that Indian businesses and professionals operate in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BRICS Summit 2026: Full Itinerary, Timings and What to Watch in New Delhi
articles.excerpt: Leaders of the expanded 11-member bloc converge on Bharat Mandapam on September 12–13, with the BRICS Business Forum opening today and traffic restrictions across central Delhi.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi speaks at a public address, with Indian national flags displayed behind him. Modi hosts the 18th BRICS Leaders’ Summit at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on September 12–13 as India holds the grouping’s 2026 chairship.
articles.nri_angle: Summit decisions on cross-border payments, national-currency settlement and digital trade set the infrastructure for cheaper remittances and more competitive Indian exporters — and mark India's bid to be a global-economic rule-maker.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Russian drones kill 2 at Ukraine-Moldova border crossing; Zelenskyy demands global action
articles.excerpt: Moscow's drones struck the Starokozache crossing in Odesa region and renewed attacks on Kyiv, a day after Russian drones violated Moldovan airspace and delayed Zelenskyy's flight to Norway.
articles.image_caption: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy arrives at an airport, greeted by officials. Zelenskyy called for global action after Russian drones killed two people at a Ukraine-Moldova border crossing.
articles.nri_angle: Prolonged disruption of Black Sea and overland trade routes keeps upward pressure on global crude and freight costs felt by NRIs, while the safety of Indians still in Ukraine is a recurring concern.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 'More or less' finalised: commerce secretary says India-US trade deal nears signing
articles.excerpt: Rajesh Agrawal said the two sides are working on a framework for preferential market access bridging India's MFN tariffs and US executive tariffs, with signing to follow at an 'appropriate time.'
articles.image_caption: A container ship being loaded at Jawaharlal Nehru Port near Mumbai, India's largest container port. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said the India-US trade deal has been 'more or less' finalised.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American businesses and exporters stand to gain preferential US market access, while NRIs could benefit if fintech-driven remittance costs fall as the commerce secretary envisions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pakistan rules out immediate military action under Mecca pact after Houthi attacks
articles.excerpt: Islamabad says no military response is under discussion following Houthi strikes on Saudi cities and energy infrastructure, but pledges it will act under the trilateral defence pact 'when time comes.'
articles.image_caption: The Great Mosque of Mecca. Pakistan says no military response is currently being discussed under the Mecca defence pact it signed with Turkey and Saudi Arabia.
articles.nri_angle: Millions of Indians live and work in Saudi Arabia and the wider Gulf; any widening of the conflict threatens their safety and remittance flows, while crude price spikes feed India's import bill.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rights groups condemn 'racist murder' of Manipuri singer in Delhi, demand racial-motive probe
articles.excerpt: Civil society and human rights organisations say the mob killing of musician Chongtham Vikram Singh must be examined in the wider context of racial violence against people from Northeast India.
articles.image_caption: A candle-lighting vigil for Chongtham Vikram, the 55-year-old Manipuri guitarist killed in Delhi. Rights groups have condemned his murder as racially motivated.
articles.nri_angle: For the Northeastern diaspora abroad, the case is a measure of how India confronts racial violence at home, shaping how safe the community feels in Indian cities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Condemns Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia as 'Unacceptable' Threat to Region
articles.excerpt: New Delhi denounced Houthi strikes on Saudi civilian and economic sites that injured 73 people, warning the escalation threatens regional stability and freedom of navigation through the Bab-el-Mandeb.
articles.image_caption: MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal speaks at a press briefing in New Delhi. India condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's civilian and economic infrastructure, which injured 73 people, as unacceptable.
articles.nri_angle: Saudi Arabia hosts one of the largest Indian expatriate communities in the world, and attacks on its oil infrastructure feed directly into crude prices that shape inflation in India.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Lancet Study: Passive Smoking Deaths in India Jump 50% Since 1990
articles.excerpt: Deaths from second-hand smoke in India rose from about 217,700 to 325,600 between 1990 and 2023, with 444 million Indians now exposed — the world's second-highest total after China.
articles.image_caption: A smoker exhales a cloud of cigarette smoke. A Lancet study finds passive-smoking deaths in India have jumped 50 percent since 1990.
articles.nri_angle: The findings matter for Indian-American multi-generational households, where grandparents visiting from India may smoke indoors and children face the greatest health burden from second-hand exposure.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bangladesh Rules Out PM Tarique Rahman's Attendance at Delhi BRICS Summit
articles.excerpt: Dhaka says the BRICS invitation was extended to the BIMSTEC chair, not to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman personally, and insists his first India visit cannot be a multilateral one.
articles.image_caption: Tarique Rahman presiding over a National Economic Council meeting in Dhaka. Bangladesh has ruled out the prime minister's attendance at the BRICS summit in New Delhi.
articles.nri_angle: The India-Bangladesh relationship is watched closely by the Bangladeshi diaspora and Indian-Americans with ties across the border; the first Rahman-Modi meeting will set the tone for trade and border issues affecting millions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: China Confirms Xi to Visit India for First Time in Seven Years
articles.excerpt: President Xi Jinping will attend the BRICS summit in New Delhi on September 12–13, with bilateral talks and a trade-minister meeting set amid record trade and a record deficit.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American and global Indian business professionals face practical stakes in the visit, from supply-chain and investment rules to visas and trade finance.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India, Russia Expand Talks on Building 105 Regional Aircraft Ahead of BRICS
articles.excerpt: Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu says New Delhi and Moscow have widened talks on manufacturing the IL-114 turboprop and Sukhoi Superjet 100 in India, targeting the UDAN regional connectivity push.
articles.image_caption: Indian and Russian officials at a signing ceremony with both countries' flags on the table. India and Russia are expanding talks on building 105 regional aircraft ahead of the BRICS summit.
articles.nri_angle: Primarily a domestic aviation and manufacturing story; it matters for NRIs who fly India's expanding regional routes and for the diaspora watching India's industrial ambitions.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Virtual Trade Corridors Could Deepen BRICS Connectivity, Says RITES Chief
articles.excerpt: RITES CMD Rahul Mithal told the BRICS Roundtable that India's MAITRI platform could seed a digital trade network across the bloc — a starting point for the Bharat Trade Net vision.
articles.nri_angle: A domestic trade-infrastructure story; relevant to NRIs in logistics, shipping and trade, and to the diaspora watching India's BRICS chairmanship.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
